mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Seoul Central District Court Registration Office or competent District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sequence for Hague member-state issuer: obtain the certified original from the District Court Registry; have a Korean notary public certify the signing official's authority if required; apply to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Division for a Hague Apostille; submit without consular legalization. For non-member-state issuer: obtain certified original; notarize; complete consular legalization by the Korean diplomatic mission; never combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Business Registration Certificate and National Tax Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service (Korean Inland Revenue counterpart)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: request certified business registration and tax clearance from the National Tax Service; have any required notarization performed; obtain a Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; no consular legalization for Apostille states. If the issuing authority is in a non-Apostille state, use consular legalization exclusively through the foreign ministry and Korean consulate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the ultimate parent company in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the board resolution and power of attorney before a notary public in the parent company's jurisdiction; if that jurisdiction is party to the Hague Apostille Convention, attach an Apostille issued by that state's designated competent authority; if not, complete consular legalization through the local foreign ministry and the Korean embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (certified copy of the parent entity's charter and the draft Korean Articles of Association)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or corporate agent of the origin state, and Korean legal counsel for the draft Korean Articles
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For the parent charter, obtain a certified copy from the corporate registry; notarize if required; obtain a Hague Apostille in the origin state. For the Korean Articles of Association, execute before a Korean notary, then file with the District Court as part of incorporation; no Vatican-style sequential authentication. For non-Apostille origin states, substitute consular legalization for the Apostille at the Korean consular post.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign shareholder or investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal relationship bank of the foreign shareholder or investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain an original signed bank reference letter on bank letterhead; notarize the authorized signatory's signature; if the bank's country is a Hague Apostille member, obtain an Apostille from that country's designated authority; if not, complete consular legalization at the Korean embassy or consulate. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be applied sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, authorized signatories and counterparties must be screened before onboarding against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit designation list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, and Korean domestic enforcement notices. The screening must also cover domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their immediate family members, close associates, negative media reports, adverse regulatory actions and high-risk jurisdictions. Enhanced due diligence with documented source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence is mandatory for a high-risk virtual card issuer. Screening must be refreshed continuously and re-performed at every ownership or control change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (Internet Registry, https://www.iros.go.kr/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean statutory naming requires registration in the Korean alphabet (Hangul). A foreign-language trade name may be used only if transliterated into Hangul, except where the registration office permits a parallel English trade name. The four-tier naming convention is: distinctive element, business-purpose descriptor, legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa, and registry clearance classification. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names, must not misrepresent the entity's business, and the Yuhan Hoesa suffix must be included in full.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed trade name, the applicant must obtain the written refusal, prepare amended Articles of Association, and within fourteen days file an objection with the competent District Court under the Commercial Registration Rules. The submission must include a cover petition, the rejected application, a certified copy of the refusal, the amended Articles, and legal argument showing the proposed name is distinguishable, not misleading, and permitted. The court issues a ruling; if adverse, the applicant may file a re-appeal under the Non-Contentious Cases Litigation Procedure Act within fourteen days. For a licensed token such as Card, Credit or Fintech, obtain prior approval from the Financial Services Commission before resubmitting.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally tolerated for non-financial holding companies, but for a high-risk virtual card issuer under the Specialized Credit Financial Business Act, the Financial Services Commission requires a substantive head office in Korea. The registered office must include a physical lease, employee presence, governance records, AML/CFT systems, and technology-security infrastructure. The National Tax Service and Korean banks reject virtual mailboxes as evidence of sham presence, which would block business registration, corporate bank account onboarding, and VAT registration. Therefore a virtual office is effectively impermissible in this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection probability is quantified at 80% within the first 12 months for a licensed virtual card issuer due to Financial Services Commission, National Tax Service, and Financial Supervisory Service monitoring. The inspection checklist includes a physical signboard, original lease contract, employee attendance and payroll records, board meeting minutes, AML compliance files, IT and data-server location, and business-registration documents. For an unlicensed holding-only Yuhan Hoesa, the probability declines to 35%, mainly from National Tax Service registration verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Sangbeob), Chapter on Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 287-2 et seq., together with the Commercial Registration Act and Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act; the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Specialized Credit Financial Business Act govern the licensed electronic payment and virtual card issuing activities where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Registry Office of the local District Court of the Republic of Korea having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; administered nationally by the National Court Administration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Commercial Registration Application filed with the District Court Registry, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation and capital deposit certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act for formation of a Yuhan Hoesa; no statutory minimum paid-in capital is required for incorporation. For the intended virtual corporate card and

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: Home Tax Service (HTS) at hometax.go.kr; export goods physical movement clearance and customs declaration acceptance are supervised by Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic customs portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Korean domestic entity Yuhan Hoesa (LLC), the Tax Identification Number (TIN) is the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) issued after incorporation under the Commercial Act. Step 1: file incorporation with the local court registry and obtain the certificate of incorporation. Step 2: apply for Business Registration (BRN) with the National Tax Service through the Home Tax portal or by visiting the competent district tax office within the statutory commencement period. Step 3: NTS accepts the application and issues the BRN certificate, which simultaneously serves as the corporate TIN and the VAT identification number for electronic tax invoices. Step 4: register for electronic tax invoice issuance in the Home Tax e-Invoice System using an NTS-accredited digital certificate. Step 5: open a corporate bank account, including a foreign-exchange repatriation account, and complete payroll and withholding tax registration with the NTS if the entity hires personnel. For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a local establishment, the domestic BRN route is unavailable; the foreign entity must instead complete simplified VAT registration through a resident tax representative using the foreigner Business Registration procedure applicable to overseas electronic service suppliers, with the representative filing returns and receiving refunds on its behalf.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Yuhan Hoesa is taxed under the Corporate Tax Act as a domestic corporation on worldwide income with no general pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; South Korea does not afford a check-the-box election for entity classification. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily treated as a separate corporate taxpayer, and no domestic statutory hybrid mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold: every Korean corporation supplying taxable goods or services must register for VAT from its first taxable supply. A de minimis annual revenue threshold of KRW 300 million applies only to foreign non-resident suppliers of electronic services under the simplified overseas businessperson VAT registration regime; below that threshold, such foreign suppliers are not required to register in Korea.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for all corporations. The Yuhan Hoesa must issue and submit tax invoices through the NTS Home Tax e-Invoice System, either directly via API or through a certified ASP before the statutory due date. Each electronic tax invoice carries a unique sequential invoice number and an NTS-generated association number, is digitally certified, and is transmitted to NTS in near-real time for fiscal validation. There is no per-transaction government digital stamping model; compliance is enforced through transactional data matching, mandatory electronic delivery to the customer, and automated cross-checks of issuance, payment, and VAT return data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAT Act, 0% VAT applies to exports of goods actually moved out of the Republic of Korea upon acceptance of an export declaration by Korea Customs Service, and to services exported to non-resident enterprises or overseas users where the service is deemed supplied offshore and is paid for in foreign currency. For the virtual card issuer's cross-border B2B SaaS and platform services, zero-rating is available for fees, interchange, or licence revenues charged to non-Korean customers where the contract with the foreign counterparty demonstrates the place of supply is outside Korea, the payment is received in foreign exchange, and the service is not physically used by a Korean-resident establishment. Payment card network settlement fees attributable to foreign banks or foreign merchants may qualify if the underlying transaction is an exported financial service; however, domestic Korean merchant services remain standard-rated at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration acceptance record from the UNI-PASS electronic customs clearance system confirming that the goods have left Korea;
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the goods or service deliverables, quantity, export country, and value;
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Master Air Waybill (air or courier) evidencing physical export movement;
Foreign Exchange Bank transaction certificate, inward remittance certificate, or foreign exchange trading record evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency;
Export clearance certificate or customs export performance confirmation issued by Korea Customs Service;

For digital or software services: service agreement, customer location evidence such as IP and log data, usage reports, and proof that the foreign counterparty is a non-resident with an offshore place of use;
If applicable, a reliable audit trail of card transaction settlement instructions from Mastercard or Visa showing the foreign acquiring or issuing bank references.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-verify export declarations, foreign-exchange receipt records, bill-of-lading data, and electronic tax invoices. If a zero-rated export is unsupported, the supply is recharacterized as taxable domestic supply and VAT is reassessed at 10% on the full consideration. NTS will claw back any output VAT refund previously granted and impose an additional tax equal to the prescribed statutory penalty for under-reported sales, false tax invoices, or failure to submit evidence; penalties generally range from 10% to 100% of the tax depending on fraud. Where proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory 180-day period without a valid extension, zero-rating is revoked and VAT is exigible with the additional tax. Criminal penalties for deliberate tax evasion or fictitious export refund claims under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act include imprisonment for up to five years and fines up to fifty times the evaded tax, plus revocation of the business registration and public disclosure measures when applicable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Information Reporting System (FEIRS)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Korean won convertibility operates under a bifurcated regime. Current account transactions, including payments for imported services, royalties, and operating expenditure, are liberalised: they may be made through a registered foreign exchange bank subject only to a FEIRS filing. Capital account transactions, however, are subject to reporting thresholds and, in certain categories, prior approval. A Yuhan Hoesa virtual card issuer receiving foreign equity capital must file an FDI report through a foreign exchange bank; the inflow is then registered and capital verification is performed by the appointed accountant. Profit remittance hurdles are manageable: a non-resident shareholder may remit dividends after audited financial statements, annual corporate tax clearance, and a board-approved dividend resolution are submitted to the remitting bank. Surrender requirements are essentially absent today, as export proceeds can be held in foreign currency accounts, but any conversion to KRW must occur through a licensed domestic bank at the prevailing market rate. The real friction for a fintech card issuer is the need to prove that every individual virtual card transaction is backed by a permissible underlying trade or service; otherwise the registration of the payment under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act can be rejected and the clearing bank will block the flow.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated and settled through a domestic foreign exchange bank within 12 months after the date of issue of the export declaration certificate. If the export is settled through a foreign currency account at a Korean bank, the bank will require a FEIRS report within 30 days of receipt. Statutory mandatory conversion ratio: 0% - there is currently no requirement to convert foreign currency export proceeds into KRW in any fixed proportion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) and Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account (FDI) and Corporate Current Account
Corporate Settlement Account, USD/EUR Correspondent Linked Account
Operational KRW Account and FX Trading Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability: Low. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, the Financial Services Commission restricts deposit-taking and settlement activities to licensed financial institutions. Offshore digital EMIs are not permitted to open Korean domiciled settlement accounts, and they are legally barred from acting as the settlement institution for KRW-denominated corporate card flows. A Yuhan Hoesa must maintain its primary treasury accounts with a licensed Korean commercial bank; offshore EMIs can only function as card program managers, never as custodian of corporate funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is effectively mandatory. The Act on Real Name Financial Transactions requires the statutory director and each ultimate beneficial owner to be identified in person before a branch official. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted as a general practice; however, a proxy bearing a notarised power of attorney may appear, and the bank will conduct a live video interview with the overseas beneficial owner before activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Korea treats non-bank corporate virtual card issuers as high-risk non-face-to-face money movement platforms, raising a presumption of unregistered remittance business under the AML/CFL Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Electronic Financial Business License issued by the Financial Services Commission, Mastercard and Visa program agreements, AML/CFL governance manual, independent annual AML audit certificate, and a supervisory statement confirming no prior administrative sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership, especially through foreign corporate shareholders and nominee directors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete beneficial ownership chart, each UBO passport and proof of residential address, notarised share transfer registers, Korean legal entity registry excerpt or equivalent foreign registry, and a certified director and beneficial owner declaration in Korean and English.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border virtual card transactions are difficult to classify and may trigger Korean export or import settlement purpose-code mismatches.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the card program transaction schema showing merchant category codes, payment networks, settlement currencies, and country of commerce; include a collateral file of sample transaction invoices and receipts and the service provider FX purpose-code mapping manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The company lacks meaningful physical substance in Korea, creating a shell-entity red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a tangible Korean office lease, payroll records, national pension and employment insurance tax filings, a resident appointed AML Compliance Officer with employment certificate, and bank statements evidencing rent, payroll, and operational payments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign equity injection must be routed only through a Korean foreign exchange bank and registered through the FEIRS and KOTRA FDI notification process. Instruct the remitting bank to use SWIFT MT103 with remittance purpose code FDI or Equity Investment and the Korean company name in field 59. Open a Capital Escrow Account for the inbound funds, then after capital verification by the appointed accountant, transfer funds to the Basic Operational KRW Account. Any deviation from the declared capital amount requires pre-approval from MOEF or a designated foreign exchange bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements settle through Korean bank SWIFT MT103 for service payments, commercial letters of credit for trade finance, and documentary collections for disclosed transactions. For KRW-denominated domestic vendor payments, use BOK-Wire and the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute KFTC; for virtual card expenditures, the clearing rails are Mastercard and Visa Direct settlement files transmitted to the acquiring bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD FX forward contracts with physical settlement supported by real underlying export or import exposure
Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts in USD/KRW executed through licensed cross-border banks to hedge KRW volatility
Dual-currency swap arrangements for actual trade-related principal flows within the transaction limits set by MOEF and the Financial Supervisory Service

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company Records; Certified Minutes Retained at Registered Office; No Regulatory Filing Required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 each year for fiscal year ended December 31 (within 3 months of fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene may allow any member to petition the court to order the meeting; directors may be subject to administrative fines under the Korean Commercial Act; persistent failure may trigger National Tax Service deemed assessments and administrative strike-off after prolonged non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 each year for the preceding calendar-year taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of unpaid tax for returns filed within one month of the deadline; 40% for non-filing or knowingly unjust returns; daily late-payment interest of 0.025% from the day after the deadline; enforced seizure of assets upon continued delinquency; criminal indictment for tax evasion exceeding KRW 300 million.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the Annual General Meeting of Members approving the financial statements; if the AGM is held on March 31, the filing is due by April 14
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the audit report may trigger administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000; the Financial Supervisory Service may order correction, impose supervisory sanctions, and require immediate auditor engagement; repeated non-compliance may lead to criminal referral and restrictions on the issuance of virtual cards.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Preliminary Return for First Half (January - June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 25 of the same taxable year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% of underpaid VAT plus 0.025% daily interest; non-filing may trigger NTS estimated assessment, seizure of bank accounts, and mandatory named disclosure as delinquent taxpayer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Final Return for First Half (January - June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 25 of the same taxable year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same as preliminary return: 10% additional tax on unpaid VAT; 0.025% daily late-payment interest; enforced collection and suspension of domestic business registration for prolonged non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Preliminary Return for Second Half (July - December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: October 25 of the same taxable year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% of unpaid VAT; daily overdue interest at 0.025%; seizure of corporate bank accounts and administrative strike-off procedures for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Final Return for Second Half (July - December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the following taxable year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10% of unpaid VAT; daily interest at 0.025%; enforced collection through seizure and public auction of corporate assets; criminal penalties for evasion exceeding certain thresholds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Specialized Credit Finance Business Annual Business Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end (by March 31 for calendar-year entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000 per violation; suspension or revocation of the specialized credit finance business license; submission of false data may trigger criminal prosecution and principal officer sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after fiscal year-end (by January 30 of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may lead to administrative fines, special inspections, and remedial orders; serious violations involve criminal penalty of up to 5 years imprisonment or fines up to KRW 50,000,000; may also trigger de-risking by payment network partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Verification of Beneficial Ownership and Shareholding Records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal Statutory Registers; KoFIU if change in beneficial ownership occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the Annual General Meeting, and within 30 days after any direct or indirect beneficial ownership change exceeding 10% or registered member change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain accurate registers carries liability for directors under the Commercial Act; failure to report beneficial ownership changes to KoFIU within 30 days may result in fines up to KRW 30,000,000 and administrative orders; willful omission can support money laundering charges.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if at least one of the following applies: (a) total assets at fiscal year-end exceed KRW 12,000,000,000; (b) total annual revenue exceeds KRW 10,000,000,000; (c) the company has 100 or more employees at fiscal year-end; or (d) the company is a licensed financial institution including an electronic virtual card issuer. Because this entity operates as a licensed virtual card issuer under the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act, it is mandatorily subjected to an annual independent audit by a certified CPA regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for financial companies and large companies; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Korean GAAP) or IFRS for SMEs is permitted for non-financial small private companies. As a licensed financial services company engaged in virtual card issuing, K-IFRS is mandatory.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual public UBO filing is required for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. However, under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, the virtual card issuer must identify and verify beneficial owners of its members and any natural person who directly or indirectly owns at least 10% or exercises de facto control. Any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) within 30 days. Annual confirmation is performed as part of the Annual General Meeting through certified shareholder register updates and the audited financial statements.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Security Interests
Minute Book of Members' and Managers' Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% on tax base up to KRW 200 million; 19% on tax base exceeding KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion; 24% on tax base exceeding KRW 20 billion (Corporate Tax Act Article 23)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME preferential rate of 9% for first KRW 200 million; free-zone incentives only for FTZ and free economic zones not applicable to fintech; R&D tax credit up to 30% of qualifying expenses; no patent box regime; general corporate deductions under Article 24-45 of the Corporate Tax Act

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 3 / Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement) filed electronically through HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing with semi-annual preliminary corporate tax returns (June 30 and December 31) for corporations whose taxable base exceeded KRW 500 million in the prior year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year end (i.e. by 31 March for a calendar-year entity); for foreign corporations without a permanent establishment, within 5 months after the fiscal year end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Tax Base Before Statutory Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate global net income computed under Korean GAAP adjusted by K-IFRS reconciliation and tax adjustment items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include intercompany card-network interchange fees and software royalty income classified as business income; foreign-source income earned through offshore marketing subsidiaries must be declared separately on Schedule A to prevent double-counting with PE profit attribution rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year net operating losses deducted against current-year taxable base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses from the same trade or business are deductible; losses forfeited if a foreign shareholder acquires more than 50% of the LLC equity within 3 years without maintaining the same business purpose; deduction limit is 80% of tax base for the current year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign income taxes paid on income earned outside the Republic of Korea eligible for relief under Article 25 of the Corporate Tax Act
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form No. 2-3 and Evidence of Foreign Tax Payment; credit capped at the Korean tax paid on the same foreign income; if the foreign withholding tax exceeds the Korean tax liability, the excess may be claimed as a deductible expense, not as a carryforward

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory reductions arising from SME incentives, employment tax credits, or investment tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A fintech corporation classified as a financial and insurance enterprise under Article 66 of the Corporate Tax Act is excluded from most SME income exemptions; only R&D tax credits for software development are available if the virtual card platform owns source code and bears CIGA

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Withholding Tax on Foreign-Domiciled Shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total withholding tax liability on dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-resident shareholders or counterparties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify beneficial ownership before applying treaty-reduced rates; the LLC must file Form Housekeeping Report No. 21 and submit Tax Residency Certificate plus board resolution proving no pass-through to third-country tax havens; failure to secure the certificate triggers the statutory 22% withholding rate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of all controlled transactions with foreign related parties, including the consideration method and arm's length adjustment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Local File documentation if annual foreign intercompany transactions exceed KRW 30 billion; disclose Mastercard/Visa network fee allocations and management service charges; mark 'A' for adjusted cost base or 'M' for internal comparables on Form No. 19-1

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 20% of the underpaid tax (Article 47-5 of the International Tax Coordination Act); additionally, failure to file an annual return with no tax due incurs KRW 500,000; overdue daily surcharge accrues at 0.05% per calendar day (3.65% annual) for up to 60 months; fraudulent omission of income or use of fabricated invoices triggers criminal prosecution under Article 12 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to 7 years and fine up to 3 times the tax evaded

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national corporation tax plus 10% local income tax surtax) levied on gross dividends remitted to non-resident shareholders under Article 98, Item 1 of the Corporate Income Tax Act and Article 45 of the Local Tax Act
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must (1) submit a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent tax authority of the residence country to the Korean withholding agent before the distribution date; (2) file a Beneficial Ownership Declaration on Form No. 40-20-1 confirming the shareholder receives the income and bears the economic risk; (3) provide a corporate board resolution and audited financial statements proving active business substance, not a conduit; (4) rely on the treaty reduction (e.g. 5% for direct holdings of at least 10% voting stock under the Korea-Singapore or Korea-Luxembourg treaties) at the moment of payment; if the Korean revenue service deems the declaration incomplete, the LLC must withhold the full 22% and the shareholder later files a refund claim through the National Tax Service's E-Tax Interface within 3 years
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate is 22% for interest and royalties paid to non-residents under Corporate Income Tax Act Article 98 (national 20% plus local 2%). Under typical Korean bilateral treaties, interest is reduced to 10% and royalties to 10% (or 15% for US treaty royalties); the reduced rate applies only upon prior submission of the TRC and beneficial ownership documents to the tax office having jurisdiction over the payor

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 30,000,000,000 (USD equivalent) of combined intercompany transactions with foreign related parties triggers mandatory Local File; group-wide consolidated turnover exceeding KRW 100,000,000,000 triggers Master File and Country-by-Country reporting under Article 111 of the International Tax Coordination Act
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies the arm's length principle under OECD BEPS Action 10; while Korea has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime, the Korean National Tax Service applies CIGA principles to attribute profit to the entity performing risk-taking, strategic decision-making, and operational card-issuance activities; a shell company with nominee directors and no local head office staff will face denial of treaty benefits and a deemed-dividend adjustment under General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Article 45 of the International Tax Coordination Act)

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Transfer Pricing Manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting interchange fees and platform revenue from virtual card transactions routed to a foreign related company, or applying an unjustified cost-plus markup on intra-group call-center services to shift taxable profit to a zero-tax jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 12: imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine not exceeding 3 times the evaded tax; additionally, the International Tax Coordination Act Article 49 authorizes the NTS to impose a false-documentation penalty of 5% of the controlled transaction value
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties under Article 11 of the National Tax Collection Act; the NTS may seize director bank accounts and freeze overseas assets; the director's personal passport may be blocked via the 'Restriction on Departure for Tax Evader' mechanism for an initial 6 months, and a criminal sentence of up to 7 years' imprisonment applies to those who sign false financial statements

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing corporate virtual cards using the Mastercard/Visa network without obtaining a statutory license from the Financial Services Commission, or failing to file cash transaction reports for card settlements exceeding KRW 10 million per transaction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Electronic Financial Transactions Act Article 49: imprisonment up to 7 years and fine up to KRW 300 million; additionally, Act for Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information Article 12 imposes a fine of up to KRW 200 million for omission of virtual currency or card settlement reports
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Financial Supervisory Service may blacklist the director from serving in any financial company; the director faces personal criminal liability including imprisonment up to 3 years for AML reporting gaps, and civil compensation to cardholders for unauthorized transactions under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act; a travel ban is imposed under Article 38 of the Act on Regulation of Financial Company Supervision

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse and Economic Substance Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Korean LLC as a virtual-card issuer solely to access the local payment network while no officers, physical office, or bank accounts exist in Korea; transactions are passed through to a South-Korean resident controlled entity abroad; the entity fails the beneficial ownership and CIGA tests under Korean corporate tax law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Coordination Act Article 45 applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule to disallow all treaty benefits and demand tax on the entire global income at the maximum 24% rate; Corporate Income Tax Act Article 121 requires non-residents to file a branch return; non-compliance triggers a punitive 35% gross tax on deemed distributions; the firm is placed on the NTS 'Fraudulent Delinquent Taxpayer' blacklist which is publicly disclosed
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil under Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Act and Article 11 of the National Tax Collection Act makes directors personally liable for 100% of unpaid tax plus penalties; directors face criminal prosecution under Article 16 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for using a sham corporation, with imprisonment up to 5 years; civil flight-risk measures include impoundment of shares, seizure of director's real estate, and travel ban until the tax debt is fully settled
